newsitem.title: USA: US stocks down at midday, bonds off.
newsitem.headline: US stocks down at midday, bonds off.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were down at midday as the bond market weakened and apprehension grew that the fourth-quarter employment-cost index, due out Tuesday, would indicate upward pressure on wages.
The Dow industrials were down 32 points at 6665, while declines led advancing issues by 14 to eight on volume of about 193 million shares.
"You came into this week with some negative momentum following last Thursday and Friday," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
The negative momentum was sustained by caution ahead of the employment data and a sagging bond market, where the 30-year Treasury was off 12/32 to yield 6.92 percent.

"There is anxiety about employment costs. We have seen some pressure on wage costs creeping up," Barthel said. "It is a moderate increase, but Wall Street is paranoid. We should get real. Japan and Germany have much higher labor costs than we do, and they don't have runaway inflation."
In addition to concern over interest rates and inflation, the market suffered as Cascade Communications Corp and related high techs resumed declines that began last week.

High tech stocks were mostly lower, with the Nasdaq Composite Index, heavily weighted with high techs, down six at 1358. Other high tech barometers were also lower, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of semiconductor issues down one at 269 and the Nasdaq 100 Index down five at 893.
Cascade was down 2-5/16 at 38-11/16, continuing a drop triggered by the release of its fourth-quarter results.

While Cascade's earnings were sharply higher versus a year ago, a fistful of analysts downgraded the shares on Friday, citing concerns over slow growth in the company's core network-switching business.
The highlight will be the first sale ever of $7.0 billion of inflation-indexed 10-year Treasury notes.

A trader at a U.S. investment bank called the issue "a little too large," adding that "unless somebody steps up to the plate in a big way at the auction, it looks like it going to be a dealer-led issue with that kind of size."

The market paid little attention to the release of a 3.5 percent drop in the December existing home sales to an annual rate of 3.87 million. Wall Street economists were expecting an average annual rate of 4.0 million.

Among special situations, shares of Measurex Corp rallied 10-3/8 to 34-5/8 after Honeywell Inc announced plans to acquire the company for $35 a share, or $600 million. Honeywell shares were down 1/4 at 69-3/4.
Compaq Computer Corp shares rallied 2-1/8 to 83-1/4. Alex. Brown upgraded Compaq to strong buy from buy.
After Raymond James Financial said it lowered its recommendation on Chicago Miniature Lamp Inc to neutral from buy, the shares fell 14-1/8 at 28-5/8.
